newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris, oil firms sign $2 bln Caspian Sea deal.
newsitem.headline: Azeris, oil firms sign $2 bln Caspian Sea deal.

text.p: Azerbaijan and a consortium of foreign oil companies led by Amoco Corp's Amoco Eurasian Petroleum Company signed a $2 billion deal on Saturday in Baku to develop the Ashrafi and Dan Ulduzu oil fields.
The 25-year contract is Azerbaijan's fourth major deal with a consortium of Western companies, in the Caucasus republic's Caspian Sea reserves.
Amoco said it hopes to sign another exploration agreement with the former Soviet republic soon.
The Western consortium in Saturday's deal includes Amoco Eurasian, with a 30 percent stake, Unocal with 25.5 percent, Japan's Itochu with 20 percent and Saudi Arabia's Delta Nimir with 4.5 percent.

The Azerbaijan state oil company SOCAR will have a 20 percent stake in the deal and Azeri oil officials say 65 to 80 percent of profits from the development of the fields will go to the Azeri government.

The Ashrafi and Dan Ulduzu fields lie appoximately 30 miles off the Apsheron peninsula. They are spread over 453 square km (175 sq miles) at depths of 75 to 200 metres (246 to 656 feet) and are estimated to contain 150 million tonnes of crude.
First production is expected to come on line in 2003 and will reach seven million tonnes per year by 2007.
The deal requires an up-front bonus payment to the Azeri government of $75 million from consortium members and must be ratified by the Azeri parliament.
The deal brings total western investment in Azerbaijan's promising oil sector to over $12 billion.
Azeri President Haydar Aliyev said the agreement was evidence of the growing importance of the former Soviet republic for American companies.
"I am happy that the Clinton administration is finding cooperation with Azerbaijan," Aliyev said, adding that he had received a telephone call from U.S. Vice President Al Gore on Friday.

"I consider that the U.S. and Azerbaijan are strategic partners... The Vice President said the administration supports cooperation with the Azeri oil sector and regards the contract as of the utmost importance," he said.
Azerbaijan, with its vast Capsian oil potential, has been the centre of a tug-of-war between Russia, Iran, Trukey and Western countries since independence in 1991.
Tom Stacy, Chairman of Amoco Eurasian Petroleum Company, said the oil giant hoped to sign another Caspian contract with the Azeri government soon.
"We are happy to work in Azerbaijan and hope to sign another contract soon on exploration of the southern part of the Azeri sector of the Caspian basin," he told a news conference.
